data.title: Conspiracy Framing Used to Immunise the Claim
data.summary:
Campaign content is framed so that denial confirms it and evidence of innocence is
presented as evidence of concealment, with a standard of proof set so that it cannot be
met.
data.description:
This framing is chosen because it removes the organisation's ability to respond. Any
denial is absorbed as expected behaviour, any disclosure is read as partial, and any
unexplained gap — of which every real organisation has many — becomes confirmation.

Recognising it matters because it determines that engagement is counter-productive. Each
response supplies new material and demonstrates that the claim is worth the
organisation's attention, which is itself treated as significant.

The honest recommendation is often that the client does nothing visible. That is an
uncomfortable thing to put in a report and should be stated plainly, with the reasoning,
rather than softened into a communications plan that will make things worse.
data.recommendation:
* Do not engage with the claim's substance; the framing converts every response into
  further evidence.
* Communicate to the unconvinced audience through routine channels rather than through
  rebuttal.
* Resist internal pressure to "answer the allegations" and record that advice explicitly,
  since it will be revisited.
data.short_recommendation: Do not engage the substance; communicate routinely to the wider audience.
